summary: WorldEntity revision validation accepts finite integer-valued doubles outside the exactly incrementable range. A record with stateRevision or representationRevision = 9007199254740992 passes assertNonNegativeInteger, but adding 1 yields the same IEEE-754 value, so capture/transition can violate the contract that successful captures/representation changes advance their revision. PR #271's new direct-boundary ownership/validation still uses this validator, so its malformed-revision closure should also reject unsafe revision counters or explicitly assert increment headroom before arithmetic.
evidence: main@914d0a2 src/shared/Reality/WorldEntity.luau assertNonNegativeInteger checks only finite, >= 0, and floor equality; it has no maximum safe-integer bound.
captureState computes stateRevision + 1 and transition computes representationRevision + 1; IEEE-754 double arithmetic has 9007199254740992 + 1 == 9007199254740992.
tests/world_entity.luau covers negative/fractional revisions but no safe-integer boundary; PR #271 adds math.huge rejection but no finite unsafe-integer case.
